Design a detailed implementation plan for the repo /home/nick/work/andesim (branch andesim). You may read any files to verify details, but do NOT modify anything.

# Task (user request)
1. Add a new `profile` subcommand to the C++ driver (`build/andesim`, sources in `driver/`). Like `--mode hybrid`, it must pick a vsim engine (default = the sole cycle-accurate engine, via the existing `resolve_accurate_engine`) and pass that engine's QEMU config to a QEMU launch.
2. Fold the functionality of the standalone `build/hotloops` binary (`driver/hotloops.cpp`, 880 lines, CMake target `hotloops` at driver/CMakeLists.txt:69) into this `profile` subcommand, so the extra binary is deleted.
3. Rename the feature "hotloops" -> "hotIterationLoop" everywhere (user decision: literal camelCase in file names and strings: `qemu_plugin/hotIterationLoop.c`, `libhotIterationLoop.so`, report title `# HotIterationLoop Report`, log prefix `hotIterationLoop:`).

# Decisions already made (do not revisit)
- CLI surface of `andesim profile`: positional ELF; `--engine ID` (optional, hybrid-style default); keep report flags `--limit`, `--min-iters`, `--raw`, `--llm/--no-llm`, `--optimize-rvv/--no-optimize-rvv`, `--no-source`, `--objdump` (Cli.objdump already exists), `--addr2line`; drop QEMU-shape flags (`--qemu`, `--plugin`, `--machine`, `--cpu`, `--qemu-config`, `--arch`, `--cwd`, `--qemu-arg`) — QEMU binary comes from the registry path (`$VSIM_QEMU`/config.env `QEMU_BIN_DIR`), cpu/vlen/readconfig from the engine probe, arch from the ELF header; extra QEMU args go through the existing `-- <args>` passthrough; also support `--mem-size` (forward as `-m`, like run_fast's qemu_m_args at cmd_run.cpp:204) and `--dry-run` (print argv, spawn nothing) and `--log-level/--log-file`.
- `docs/hotloops.md` is rewritten as `docs/profile.md`.
- The TCG plugin stays a separate .so (required by QEMU); only the driver-side standalone binary is deleted.
- Old hotloops ignored QEMU's exit code entirely; new behavior: hard-error if the QEMU spawn fails, log a warning if guest rc != 0 but still produce the report.

# Verified facts from exploration (line numbers checked today)
## Current hotloops
- qemu_plugin/hotloops.c (179 lines): TCG plugin, args `limit=` (default 50) `min_iters=` (default 1, 0 clamped to 1), detects backward TB transitions, on exit emits via qemu_plugin_outs(): header `hotloops: N distinct backward edges, M hot (>= K iters)...`, then CSV rows `0x%016x, 0x%016x, %u` (start_pc, end_pc, iters). Driver captures via `-d plugin -D <logfile>`.
- driver/hotloops.cpp flow: parse_args (:119-156) -> detect_arch from ELF header (:160-170) -> locate qemu (:724-739, own narrower logic NOT honoring $VSIM_QEMU) -> locate plugin (:742-751) -> mkstemp log (:59-71) -> QEMU argv (:756-772): `{qemu, -plugin, <so>,limit=N,min_iters=M, -d, plugin, -D, <log>, -M, andes_ae350, -cpu, <cpu>, -nographic, -semihosting, -bios, <elf>}` + optional -readconfig + extra args -> run_silent (stdio to /dev/null, rc ignored) -> parse_log regex `(0x...),(0x...),(\d+)` (:291-307) -> objdump disasm map (:793-828, prefers $HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN) -> filter (min_iters, RVV-only via mnemonic starts with 'v', sort desc, truncate limit) (:830-848) -> addr2line source resolution (:850-869) -> print_llm (markdown report with per-loop `function:`, `measure: --pc-start 0x.. --pc-end 0x..`, `source:`, `code:`, `rvv:`, nesting parent/children via PC-range containment build_loops :463-494) or print_table (:503-563). Exit 2 only for CLI/setup errors.
- It reuses driver units already: elf_syms.cpp (symbolize, fn_range), process.cpp (run_process), repo_root.hpp.
- Zero unit tests. One manual shell test tests/plugin/test_plugin_hotloops_measure.sh (89 lines): builds RVV vadd fixture against vplat runtime, runs `build/hotloops --min-iters 10`, asserts `[hottest]` + `measure:` line, cross-checks --pc-start/--pc-end against nm/objdump oracle of vadd_kernel. NOT wired into any runner (tests/plugin/ is manual-only by convention, same as tests/andes_sim/ which IS run by scripts/test_all.sh contract phase — verify: test_all.sh:85-86 runs tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh + tests/andes_csr/test_*.sh only).
## Driver CLI
- cli.cpp:29-31 `is_subcommand` = run|list|doctor; default-to-run at :45-51; global option parse (match_opt :11-25, bools :56-80, value opts :82-96: --mode/--engine/--trigger/--pc-start/--pc-end/--mem-size/--mmap-size/--kanata/--objdump/--log-level/--log-file/--gdb-port). Cli struct at cli.hpp:29-54 (has objdump, mem_size, passthrough, dry_run, verify, help, error...).
- main.cpp: fwd decls :18-20, help tables kRunModes :43-47 kRunOpts :71-88, print_run_block :110-118, print_list_block :120-126, print_doctor_block :128-130, print_usage :134-148, print_subcommand_help :152-156, dispatch :196-198.
- Engine path: engine_descriptor.hpp:25-53 (ilm_size/dlm_size/hvm_size, vlen, xlen, invoke templates; NO qemu_cpu/readconfig fields — those come from runtime probe). engine_registry.hpp:77-119 resolve_accurate_engine (explicit --engine must exist + be cycle-accurate; empty defaults to sole accurate engine, errors on zero/many). engine_registry.cpp:193-216 discover_engines ($ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR override or $VSIM_BIN_DIR sim_* scan, probe --describe / .json sidecar). builtin_qemu_arch engine_registry.cpp:30-86 (fast-leg + standalone invoke templates; QEMU binary resolution :76-84 $VSIM_QEMU -> config.env QEMU_BIN_DIR -> repo_root()/build/qemu/...).
- QEMU-cfg probe helpers (exported in run_plan.hpp:73-85, defined run_plan.cpp): stage_qemu_cfg (:144-152 writes workdir/qemu.cfg), qemu_cpu_from_cfg (:126-142 parses `driver = "<cpu>-riscv-cpu"`), used by run_plan :388-396 (probe `<engine> --print-qemu-config` with kQemuCfgProbeMs timeout) and by cmd_run.cpp:479-487 (--print-memmap branch calls them directly - the pattern to copy). -readconfig appended fast-leg only at run_plan.cpp:306-309. plugin_args suffix built at :279-281 with ilm_size/dlm_size/hvm_size from engine descriptor.
- cmd_run.cpp run_hybrid :369-656 (engine resolve at :457-465, hw check :469, elf/engine arch check elf_engine_arch_error :471); run_fast :192-233 (qemu_m_args :204).
- process.hpp: run_process (capture, timeout), exec_passthrough, run_line_filtered. log.hpp: log_line levels to stderr, log_result stdout.
## Tests
- Unit framework: driver/test_check.hpp (CHECK macro + report(), each test its own main). CMakeLists.txt:47-66 one add_executable per test linking only units under test; outputs to build/driver; run by scripts/test_all.sh unit phase (:58-75 runs build/driver/andesim-*-test).
- cli_test.cpp (parser cases), run_test.cpp:91-142 (resolve_accurate_engine branches), plan_test.cpp:243-323 (stage_qemu_cfg/qemu_cpu_from_cfg/argv assembly coverage).
- Shell contract convention: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh, e.g. test_andes_sim_dry_run.sh (build driver, run --dry-run, grep argv fragments, SKIP when no vsim engine), test_andes_sim_f8.sh (fake engines via mkengine + ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR answering --describe with JSON, expect-rc/regex helper, then guarded real-vsim layer).
## Rename scope (from grep)
- qemu_plugin/hotloops.c (file + "hotloops:" strings :129 :168), qemu_plugin/Makefile (:16 :33 :42-44 :47), scripts/build_qemu_plugin.sh (:4 :11), driver/hotloops.cpp (file itself deleted), driver/CMakeLists.txt (:68-73 hotloops target - deleted), docs/hotloops.md (renamed to docs/profile.md, fix stale `pc_range:` examples - code now emits `function:` + `measure:`), docs/USER_GUIDE.md (:216 :221 :644 :664), README.md:45, CLAUDE.md:59, tests/plugin/test_plugin_hotloops_measure.sh (file + 14 refs). EXCLUDE docs/MRD.md:213 (unrelated "hot loop" prose) and untracked COMMIT_REFACTOR_PLAN.md.
- setup.sh:119 `make -C qemu_plugin` builds both .so via `all` target (no name reference; only Makefile changes).

# Hard constraints (project rules)
- TDD is mandatory: every behavioral change needs a failing test FIRST (RED), then minimal code (GREEN), then refactor. Unit tests use test_check.hpp convention.
- Tidy First: structural commits (renames, moves, extractions) strictly separated from behavioral commits; structural first; run tests before/after each.
- Never mix the rename (structural) with the new profile behavior (behavioral) in one commit.
- Prefer "remove and rewrite" over patching legacy code: hotloops.cpp's logic should be ported into a fresh, testable unit (e.g. driver/profile_report.{hpp,cpp} pure functions + driver/cmd_profile.cpp orchestration), then driver/hotloops.cpp deleted. Don't leave the old file.
- docs/USER_GUIDE.md must be updated whenever behavior changes.
- Simple English in docs (user is ESL).

# What I want from you
A step-by-step implementation plan:
1. Exact commit sequence, each tagged (structural) or (behavioral), each with: files touched, what tests are written first (name the test file + representative CHECK cases), the minimal implementation, and how to run the relevant test subset (scripts/build_driver.sh + which build/driver/andesim-*-test binaries, scripts/test_all.sh phases).
2. Proposed decomposition of the ported code: which functions from hotloops.cpp go into which new file, what their testable signatures should look like (e.g. parse_log(string)->vector<LoopEdge>, filter_loops(...), build_loops(...), render_llm(...)->string, profile_qemu_argv(...)->vector<string>), so unit tests can cover them without QEMU. Note print_* currently write to stdout directly - plan the refactor to return strings.
3. The cmd_profile.cpp orchestration flow (engine resolve -> probe -> argv -> spawn -> parse -> report), including workdir/tempfile handling (mkdtemp like run_plan.cpp:360-371 vs mkstemp), --dry-run output shape (mirror run's `dry-run: N command(s)` banner from run_passthrough/run_plan - check exact format), and error paths.
4. CLI/help/usage integration details (new Cli fields with defaults, kProfileOpts help rows, print_profile_block, is_subcommand, dispatch).
5. The plugin rename commit mechanics (git mv, Makefile rule, string prefix, README/CLAUDE.md bullets) and the shell-test port (tests/plugin/test_plugin_hotIterationLoop_measure.sh invoking `./andesim profile`).
6. New contract test tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_profile.sh design (fake-engine --describe + --print-qemu-config answers, --dry-run argv assertions, engine-resolution error branches, guarded real-vsim+real-QEMU layer).
7. docs plan (docs/profile.md structure, USER_GUIDE.md new section placement after section 5, README/CLAUDE.md build-output bullet updates).
8. Verification section: end-to-end manual check commands (real engine + RVV fixture, assert report sanity), and the full test_all.sh run.
9. Risks/gotchas: e.g. Cli global parse means new flags visible to run (decide: cmd_run rejects them? or ignore - check how run treats unknown-to-it Cli fields today, e.g. does cmd_list reject --engine? find the existing convention validate-per-command), --raw vs --llm interaction, the probe running under --dry-run (engine spawn is OK in dry-run? mirror run_plan behavior), rv32 ELF + rv64 engine mismatch (reuse elf_engine_arch_error), engines whose --print-qemu-config fails (run_plan treats probe failure how? check :388-396 error path), $HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN objdump fallback chain.
Answer with the complete plan, concrete and self-contained (I will merge it into the final plan file). Cite file:line for every claim you verify in the repo.

1	// andesim command-line parsing.
2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andesim [<cmd>] [--mode M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// `run` is the default command: when the first token is not a known
9	// subcommand (and not a top-level help flag), the whole line parses as
10	// `run ...`, so `andesim --mode fast prog.elf` works without typing `run`.
11	//
12	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
13	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
14	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`cycle` forward an engine's whole
15	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.
16	#ifndef ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
17	#define ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
18	
19	#include <string>
20	#include <string_view>
21	#include <vector>
22	
23	namespace andes_sim {
24	
25	// True for the known command names (run/list/doctor). The single source of
26	// truth shared by the parser (default-command rule) and main's dispatch.
27	bool is_subcommand(std::string_view name);
28	
29	struct Cli {
30	  std::string subcommand;                 // e.g. "run", "list"; "" if none
31	  std::string model;                      // --mode fast|cycle|hybrid (field stays 'model': the concept, see list models)
32	  std::string engine;                     // --engine <id>
33	  std::string trigger;                    // --trigger marker|pc
34	  // Hybrid trigger args (empty => cmd_run applies the default). pc boundaries
35	  // are a symbol name or 0x address; the sizes stay strings here and are
36	  // parsed where they are used.
37	  std::string pc_start;                   // --pc-start (trigger pc)
38	  std::string pc_end;                     // --pc-end   (trigger pc)
39	  std::string mem_size;                   // --mem-size (guest memory; --mmap-size is a hidden alias)
40	  std::string kanata;                     // --kanata <file> (marker/pc ROI trace)
41	  std::string objdump;                    // --objdump <file> (kanata labels)
42	  std::string log_level;                  // --log-level 0..6 (vsim scale; "" => info)
43	  std::string log_file;                   // --log-file <path> (full trace capture)
44	  std::vector<std::string> positional;    // non-flag framework args
45	  std::vector<std::string> passthrough;   // verbatim, everything after `--`
46	  bool help = false;                      // -h / --help (before `--`)
47	  bool dry_run = false;                   // --dry-run (build, run, test, ...)
48	  bool print_memmap = false;              // --print-memmap (run --mode hybrid)
49	  bool verify = false;                    // --verify (run --mode hybrid)
50	  bool gdb = false;                       // --gdb (fast: QEMU gdbstub; cycle: vsim JTAG + ICEman)
51	  std::string gdb_port;                   // --gdb-port (fast: default 1234; cycle: default 9104)
52	  bool has_passthrough = false;           // a `--` boundary was present
53	  std::string error;                      // non-empty => parse failed
54	};
55	
56	// Parse argv[1..] (program name skipped). The vector overload is the testable
57	// core; the argv overload adapts it for main().
58	Cli parse_cli(const std::vector<std::string>& args);
59	Cli parse_cli(int argc, char** argv);
60	
61	}  // namespace andes_sim
62	
63	#endif  // ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
64

1	// The phase-plan executor (F6) -- there is no QEMU2 handback leg.
2	// run_plan spawns each leg of a Plan in order,
3	// threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward (leg N's --handoff-out is
4	// leg N+1's --resume-from-qemu), and reports each leg's mcycle/minstret.
5	//
6	// plan_argvs is the pure core (no spawn, no mmap): it resolves each Step's
7	// engine + role against the registry and fills the invoke template with the
8	// threaded state paths, so the argv construction is unit-testable in isolation.
9	#ifndef ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
10	#define ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
11	
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
16	#include "plan.hpp"
17	#include "process.hpp"
18	
19	namespace andes_sim {
20	
21	// The framework-owned values shared by every leg of a run: the resolved
22	// shared-mmap path/size/base and the QEMU plugin path. Per-leg values
23	// (bin/state_in/state_out) are derived by plan_argvs from this + the threading.
24	struct RuntimeCtx {
25	  std::string mmap_path;
26	  long long mem_size = 0;
27	  std::string mmap_base = "0x0";
28	  std::string plugin_path;
29	  // QEMU `-readconfig` file matching the accurate engine's ISA, distilled from
30	  // its config.inc (the engine's `--print-qemu-config`). Empty => the fast leg
31	  // keeps its descriptor's default `-cpu` (engines without the flag; FA2).
32	  std::string qemu_cfg;
33	  // The QEMU CPU model the fast leg must instantiate ({qemu_cpu} fill),
34	  // parsed from the same probe's `driver = "<cpu>-riscv-cpu"` globals: the
35	  // readconfig globals only apply to THAT driver, and a mismatched model
36	  // silently ignores them (found live: andes-ax45mpv kept vlen=512 when the
37	  // ax66 run asked for 128). Empty => the family default (andes-ax45mpv).
38	  std::string qemu_cpu;
39	};
40	
41	// hw-config sync: the QEMU fast leg models the hardware the accurate-leg
42	// engine measures, so its -cpu vlen follows that engine's descriptor. 512 is
43	// the fallback for engines that report none. One definition, used by both the
44	// plan executor ({vlen} fill) and the hybrid banner.
45	inline long synced_vlen(long engine_vlen) {
46	  return engine_vlen > 0 ? engine_vlen : 512;
47	}
48	
49	// A trigger's per-leg argv contribution, dispatched by the leg's role. The
50	// QEMU plugin takes its trigger as a comma-suffix folded INTO the one `-plugin`
51	// token (so it rides the `{trigger}` placeholder); vsim takes separate tokens
52	// appended to its argv. marker contributes nothing (plugin/vsim detect the markers
53	// themselves).
54	struct LegTriggerArgs {
55	  std::string plugin_suffix;        // qemu fast-leg: appended to {trigger}
56	  std::vector<std::string> extra;   // vsim accurate-leg: appended tokens
57	};
58	
59	// Map `t` onto `role`'s argv contribution. marker -> empty. pc -> qemu
60	// `,enter_pc=<enter_pc>` / vsim `--hybrid-exit-pc <exit_pc>`. Roles other
61	// than fast-leg/accurate-leg get nothing. A missing required param or an
62	// unknown trigger kind sets `err` (and returns an empty contribution).
63	//
64	// NOTE (altitude debt): these flag spellings are framework-side per-engine
65	// knowledge -- the one place F9 hardcodes a fast/accurate engine's CLI, unlike
66	// the base argv which comes from each engine's `--describe` invoke template.
67	// This is a deliberate scope cut: the principled form (per-(trigger,role) argv
68	// templates carried in `--describe`, filled by build_argv like `invoke`) would
69	// extend the F2 engine contract and is left for a later feature.
70	LegTriggerArgs leg_trigger_args(const Trigger& t, const std::string& role,
71	                                std::string& err);
72	
73	// Turn an accurate engine's `<bin> --print-qemu-config` probe into a QEMU
74	// `-readconfig` file under `workdir`. On a clean probe (exit 0, non-empty
75	// stdout) writes `workdir/qemu.cfg` and returns its path; on any failure
76	// (engine without the flag -> the parser throws -> non-zero exit; timeout;
77	// spawn failure; empty output; unwritable dir) returns "" -- the tolerant
78	// fallback that leaves the fast leg on its descriptor's default -cpu.
79	std::string stage_qemu_cfg(const std::string& workdir, const RunResult& probe);
80	
81	// The QEMU CPU model named by a `--print-qemu-config` probe's text: the first
82	// `driver = "<cpu>-riscv-cpu"` global, stripped of the "-riscv-cpu" suffix.
83	// "" when the text names none (probe failed / engine without the hook) -- the
84	// caller falls back to the family-default -cpu.
85	std::string qemu_cpu_from_cfg(const std::string& cfg_text);
86	
87	// Build every step's concrete argv, threading state files under `workdir`:
88	//   state_in[0]  = ""                       (cold start; no resume)
89	//   state_in[i]  = state_out[i-1]           (prior leg's drain)
90	//   state_out[i] = workdir/"state-<i>.bin"  (this leg's drain)
91	// Each step's engine is looked up in `engines` by id and its `role` template is
92	// filled via build_argv. Pure (no spawn). Returns one argv per step; on any
93	// error (unknown engine/role, unresolved placeholder) returns {} and sets `err`.
94	std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> plan_argvs(
95	    const Plan& plan, const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
96	    const std::string& workdir, const RuntimeCtx& ctx, std::string& err);
97	
98	// The exit code a leg returns after draining its state and handing off (the
99	// driver-side mirror of vsim's kExitHandoffToQemu). Every plan step is a drain
100	// step, so this is the expected per-leg exit.
101	constexpr int kDrainRc = 200;
102	
103	struct PlanOptions {
104	  int timeout_ms = 90000;     // per-leg spawn timeout
105	  int expect_rc = kDrainRc;   // drain success code
106	  std::string plugin_path;    // "" => $VSIM_PLUGIN else repo default
107	  bool dry_run = false;       // build argvs (incl. qemu_cfg) but spawn nothing
108	};
109	
110	// Compose the "plan step N exited wrong" diagnostic. A drain step (expect_rc is
111	// the handoff/drain code) that exits 0 ran the ELF to completion without ever
112	// reaching its ROI boundary -- the marker/pc trigger never fired; say so and
113	// name the trigger kind so the fix (right ELF / right --trigger) is obvious.
114	// Any other mismatch gets the plain "expected X, got Y" line.
115	std::string plan_step_rc_error(size_t step, const Step& s, int expect_rc,
116	                               int got_rc);
117	
118	// Execute `plan`: resolve the plugin, acquire the shared mmap (allocate one
119	// under /dev/shm when plan.mmap_path is empty, and own it), spawn each leg with
120	// a timeout, require exit == expect_rc, and read back each leg's mcycle/minstret
121	// from its drained state file. Returns the per-leg results; on the first failure
122	// `error` describes it and `phases` holds whatever completed before it.
123	PlanResult run_plan(const Plan& plan,
124	                    const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
125	                    const PlanOptions& opts = {});
126	
127	}  // namespace andes_sim
128	
129	#endif  // ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# build/hotloops LLM report contract: each loop block carries a ready hybrid
3	# pc window, `measure: --pc-start 0x<entry> --pc-end 0x<ret>`, derived from
4	# the loop's enclosing function (one-shot pc triggers fire on the first hit,
5	# so the function span covers every iteration and needs no objdump step).
6	#
7	# Invokes the tool WITHOUT --plugin so the default plugin path
8	# (qemu_plugin/libhotloops.so) is exercised end-to-end.
9	#
10	# Builds a tiny single-ret RVV kernel (vplat runtime), runs the detector,
11	# and checks the measure line against the toolchain's own nm/objdump as
12	# the oracle.
13	
14	set -uo pipefail
15	
16	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
17	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
18	
19	. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null || true
20	QEMU_BIN="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
21	GCC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"
22	NM="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm"
23	OBJDUMP="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump"
24	HOTLOOPS="$ROOT/build/hotloops"
25	
26	[ -x "$QEMU_BIN" ] || { echo "SKIP: external qemu not found (source ./setup.sh)"; exit 0; }
27	[ -f "$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhotloops.so" ] || { echo "SKIP: hotloops plugin not built (make -C qemu_plugin)"; exit 0; }
28	[ -x "$GCC" ] || { echo "SKIP: no riscv toolchain"; exit 0; }
29	[ -d "$ROOT/build/runtime" ] || { echo "SKIP: vplat runtime not built"; exit 0; }
30	[ -x "$HOTLOOPS" ] || bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1
31	[ -x "$HOTLOOPS" ] || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: build/hotloops missing"; exit 1; }
32	
33	TMP=$(mktemp -d -t hotloops-measure.XXXXXX)
34	trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
35	
36	cat > "$TMP/vadd.c" <<'EOF'
37	#include <stdint.h>
38	#include <riscv_vector.h>
39	static int32_t a[64], b[64];
40	__attribute__((noinline)) static void vadd_kernel(void)
41	{
42	  for (int r = 0; r < 50; r++)
43	    for (int i = 0; i < 64;) {
44	      size_t vl = __riscv_vsetvl_e32m1((size_t) (64 - i));
45	      vint32m1_t va = __riscv_vle32_v_i32m1(&a[i], vl);
46	      vint32m1_t vb = __riscv_vle32_v_i32m1(&b[i], vl);
47	      __riscv_vse32_v_i32m1(&a[i], __riscv_vadd_vv_i32m1(va, vb, vl), vl);
48	      i += (int) vl;
49	    }
50	}
51	int main(void) { vadd_kernel(); return 0; }
52	EOF
53	
54	"$GCC" -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
55	  -B "$ROOT/build/runtime" -specs=andesim.specs \
56	  "$TMP/vadd.c" -o "$TMP/vadd.elf" \
57	  || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: fixture build failed"; exit 1; }
58	
59	# NO --plugin: the tool must resolve qemu_plugin/libhotloops.so itself.
60	REPORT=$("$HOTLOOPS" \
61	           --qemu "$QEMU_BIN" \
62	           --cpu "andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=512" \
63	           --min-iters 10 "$TMP/vadd.elf" 2>/dev/null)
64	
65	echo "$REPORT" | grep -q "\[hottest\]" \
66	  || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: no hottest loop reported"; echo "$REPORT"; exit 1; }
67	
68	MEASURE=$(echo "$REPORT" | grep -m1 "^measure:")
69	[ -n "$MEASURE" ] \
70	  || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: no measure: line in the report"; echo "$REPORT"; exit 1; }
71	
72	GOT_S=$(echo "$MEASURE" | grep -o -- "--pc-start 0x[0-9a-f]*" | awk '{print $2}')
73	GOT_E=$(echo "$MEASURE" | grep -o -- "--pc-end 0x[0-9a-f]*" | awk '{print $2}')
74	
75	# Oracle: the kernel's entry from nm; its return = the function's last
76	# instruction (single-epilogue at -O1; objdump flavors disagree on the
77	# `ret` vs `c.jr ra` spelling, so match by position, not mnemonic).
78	WANT_S=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$("$NM" "$TMP/vadd.elf" | awk '$3=="vadd_kernel"{print $1; exit}')")
79	WANT_E=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$TMP/vadd.elf" \
80	  | sed -n '/<vadd_kernel>:/,/^$/p' | grep -E '^[ ]+[0-9a-f]+:' \
81	  | tail -1 | awk '{sub(":","",$1); print $1}')")
82	
83	if [ "$GOT_S" != "$WANT_S" ] || [ "$GOT_E" != "$WANT_E" ]; then
84	  echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: window $GOT_S..$GOT_E, want $WANT_S..$WANT_E"
85	  echo "$MEASURE"
86	  exit 1
87	fi
88	
89	echo "PASS[hotloops_measure]: measure = $GOT_S .. $GOT_E (all of vadd_kernel), default plugin path OK"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F8 contract: `run --mode cycle` -- one cycle-accurate engine alone, from
# reset (no QEMU, no --resume-from-qemu), transparent passthrough. Layers:
#
#   1. run-test (unit, fast): resolve_accurate_engine's selection branches
#      (default-sole / explicit / ambiguous / missing / wrong-kind) + the F7
#      passthrough_argv assembly. Pure, no spawn.
#   2. fake-engine resolution + exec (no real vsim): a handful of throwaway
#      "engine" scripts that answer `--describe` with JSON and echo a marker
#      when run. Drives the real discover -> resolve -> run_standalone -> exec
#      path end to end. Proves the done-when "selecting a different built <cfg>
#      runs the other binary" deterministically, plus every error path. The
#      fakes ship the SAME standalone template real vsim does ({bin} {elf}), so
#      this exercises the exact argv path.
#   3. real vsim (guarded, best-effort): if a sim_<cfg> is built, invoke it
#      from reset and look for its native "N cycles simulated" line. Standalone
#      from-reset of a hybrid-oriented fixture is environment-dependent, so a
#      timeout or a missing cycle line is a skip, not a failure -- layer 2 is
#      the deterministic proof.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
RUNTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-run-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit: resolution branches + passthrough argv
[ -x "$RUNTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $RUNTEST"

# --- fixtures: throwaway engine scripts in a scanned dir --------------------
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# mkengine DIR FILE ID KIND MARKER: a fake engine that self-describes as KIND
# and, when run standalone, echoes RAN:MARKER so we can see which binary ran.

  local f="$1/$2"
  cat >"$f" <<EOF

if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then

else
  echo "RAN:$5 args:\$*"
fi
EOF
  chmod +x "$f"
}

D1="$TMP/one"; D2="$TMP/two"; DF="$TMP/func"; DE="$TMP/empty"
mkdir -p "$D1" "$D2" "$DF" "$DE"
mkengine "$D1" v1 "vsim:v1" cycle-accurate m1
mkengine "$D2" v1 "vsim:v1" cycle-accurate m1

# expect: assert rc + output regex (shared helper from tests/lib/log.sh)

# 2a. default = the sole cycle-accurate engine; it runs with the ELF appended

  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode cycle "$DUMMY"

expect 0 'RAN:m2' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine vsim:v2 "$DUMMY"

  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" run --mode cycle dummy.elf
# 2e. --engine names a functional engine: wrong kind for cycle
expect 2 'cycle-accurate' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DF" "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine vsim:f0 dummy.elf
# 2f. --engine matches nothing discovered
expect 2 "no engine 'vsim:nope'" \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine vsim:nope dummy.elf
# 2g. the shared standalone spine still rejects a missing ELF / extra positional
expect 2 'missing ELF' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode cycle
expect 2 'engine args go after --' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode cycle a.elf b.elf

      || fail "real cycle: the program's own output was dropped:"$'\n'"$out"

      fi
    done

  fi

1	// ELF symbol resolution for pc-trigger boundaries (F9).
2	//
3	// pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs. Either boundary may be a
4	// "0x"-prefixed hex address (used verbatim) OR a symbol defined in the ELF
5	// (resolved against its .symtab). This decouples the switch points from the
6	// workload source -- any function can bound the ROI, with no planted markers.
7	//
8	// C++ port of tests/lib/roi.sh:resolve_pc, reading the ELF .symtab directly via
9	// <elf.h> rather than shelling out to `nm`.
10	#ifndef ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
11	#define ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
12	
13	#include <cstdint>
14	#include <string>
15	
16	namespace andes_sim {
17	
18	// Resolve a pc-mode boundary to a bare hex address string (no "0x" prefix).
19	//   "0x<h>" / "0X<h>"  -> "<h>" verbatim (prefix stripped, digits unchanged)
20	//   <symbol>           -> the symbol's st_value as lowercase hex
21	// On any failure (undefined symbol, unreadable/!ELF file) returns "" and sets
22	// `err` to a message naming the boundary; on success leaves `err` empty.
23	std::string resolve_pc(const std::string& elf_path, const std::string& boundary,
24	                       std::string& err);
25	
26	// The ELF class width in bits from e_ident[EI_CLASS]: 32 (ELFCLASS32) or 64
27	// (ELFCLASS64). Returns 0 when `elf_path` is unreadable or not an ELF. Reads
28	// only the 16-byte e_ident (the class-independent prefix), so it answers for
29	// rv32 and rv64 alike -- the source of truth for the fast auto-pick of
30	// qemu-system-riscv32/64 and the cycle/hybrid arch-match guard.
31	int elf_xlen(const std::string& elf_path);
32	
33	// L26/F3: the highest byte of the ELF's static memory image -- the maximum
34	// (p_paddr + p_memsz) over PT_LOAD segments. The driver rejects a hybrid run
35	// when this exceeds the V-scratch GPA (ram_base + --mem-size): the static image
36	// would extend into the reserved transport page above the program's RAM.
37	// Returns 0 + err on an unreadable / non-ELFCLASS64 file; 0 with empty err when
38	// the ELF has no loadable segments (nothing to clash with the scratch).
39	uint64_t elf_load_top(const std::string& elf_path, std::string& err);
40	
41	// Reverse lookup: the nearest function symbol at or below `addr`, formatted
42	// "name+0xoff" (or just "name" at offset 0). Returns "" when no covering
43	// function symbol is found or the ELF is unreadable -- the caller always has
44	// the raw pc to fall back on, so this never errors.
45	std::string symbolize(const std::string& elf_path, uint64_t addr);
46	
47	// Returns {st_value, st_value + st_size} for the FUNC symbol covering `addr`.
48	// Both members are 0 when not found or unreadable.
49	std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t> fn_range(const std::string& elf_path, uint64_t addr);
50	
51	}  // namespace andes_sim
52	
53	#endif  // ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
54

1	// Subprocess helpers for andesim.
2	//
3	// run_process spawns a child, captures its stdout, and kills it after a
4	// timeout -- the primitive the engine registry uses to ask `<bin> --describe`
5	// and the plan executor (F6) uses to run orchestrated legs. F5 extends this
6	// file with exec_passthrough (inherit stdio, no timeout) for fast/cycle.
7	#ifndef ANDESIM_PROCESS_HPP
8	#define ANDESIM_PROCESS_HPP
9	
10	#include <functional>
11	#include <string>
12	#include <string_view>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	namespace andes_sim {
16	
17	struct RunResult {
18	  int rc = -1;                // child exit status, or -1 if killed/abnormal
19	  std::string out;            // captured stdout
20	  bool timed_out = false;     // killed because it exceeded the timeout
21	  bool spawn_failed = false;  // pipe/fork failed before the child ran
22	};
23	
24	// Run argv (argv[0] resolved via PATH), capturing stdout. The child's stdin
25	// is redirected to /dev/null; stderr too, unless relay_stderr is set, in
26	// which case the child inherits OUR stderr and its diagnostics stream live
27	// (used to surface the legs' leveled logs at --log-level <= debug). If the
28	// child runs longer than timeout_ms it is SIGKILLed and timed_out is set.
29	RunResult run_process(const std::vector<std::string>& argv, int timeout_ms,
30	                      bool relay_stderr = false);
31	
32	// Run argv to completion with the child INHERITING all three std streams
33	// (stdin, stdout, stderr) -- the transparent-passthrough mechanism behind
34	// `run --mode fast|cycle`: the engine reads/writes the terminal directly,
35	// so an interactive gdbstub or semihosting console works unchanged. No chdir,
36	// no capture, no timeout. Returns the child's exit code, 128+signal if it was
37	// signalled, or -1 on spawn failure / empty argv.
38	int exec_passthrough(const std::vector<std::string>& argv);

40	// Fork a child that execs argv with inherited stdio and return immediately
41	// without waiting. Used by `run --mode cycle --gdb` to launch vsim in the
42	// background before exec-ing ICEman in the foreground. Returns the child pid
43	// on success, -1 on empty argv or fork failure.
44	int fork_background(const std::vector<std::string>& argv);

47	// inherited, streaming each complete line to `on_line(stream, line)` as it
48	// arrives -- stream is 1 (stdout) or 2 (stderr), line excludes the trailing
49	// newline. The callback owns presentation (it decides what to write to the real
50	// streams), so this is the filtered counterpart to exec_passthrough: same "run
51	// to completion, no timeout, propagate exit code" contract, but the parent sees
52	// every line. A final unterminated line is delivered too. Returns the child's
53	// exit code, 128+signal if signalled, or -1 on spawn failure / empty argv.
54	int run_line_filtered(
55	    const std::vector<std::string>& argv,
56	    const std::function<void(int stream, std::string_view line)>& on_line);
57	
58	}  // namespace andes_sim
59

1	# hotloops - hot inner-loop detector
2	
3	Detects the hottest loops in a baremetal RISC-V ELF by observing backward
4	translation-block transitions in `qemu-system-<arch>`. For each detected
5	loop you get the loop header PC, the backward-branch PC, and the iteration
6	count. With DWARF, you also get the source `file:line`. With objdump
7	present, you get RVV-only filtering and per-loop disassembly context.
8	
9	Two parts ship together:
10	
11	- `qemu_plugin/hotloops.c` - QEMU TCG plugin that records edges.
12	- `build/hotloops` - C++ tool (source `driver/hotloops.cpp`) that runs the
13	  plugin and formats output.
14	
15	## Usage
16	
17	```
18	build/hotloops [options] <elf>
19	```
20	
21	The tool launches `qemu-system-<arch>` with `-bios <elf>` on a baremetal
22	machine (default `andes_ae350`) and a vector-capable CPU (default
23	`andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024`). Override per the options below
24	for other targets.
25	
26	### Options
27	
28	| Flag                | Default            | Description                                                    |
29	|---------------------|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
30	| `--arch <a>`        | auto               | Target arch: `riscv32`, `riscv64`, or `auto` (from `file`).    |
31	| `--qemu <path>`     | auto               | Override the `qemu-system-<arch>` binary.                      |
32	| `--plugin <path>`   | auto               | Override the plugin `.so`.                                     |
33	| `--machine <name>`  | `andes_ae350`      | `-M <name>` passed to QEMU.                                    |
34	| `--cpu <spec>`      | `andes-ax45mpv,...`| `-cpu <spec>` passed to QEMU. Default enables RVV 1.0 vlen=1024.|
35	| `--qemu-config <f>` | -                  | `-readconfig <file>` (e.g. AE350 device cfg).                  |
36	| `--cwd <dir>`       | -                  | `chdir` before launching QEMU (so semihosting `fread` of `bin/*.bin` resolves). |
37	| `--qemu-arg <arg>`  | -                  | Extra arg appended to the QEMU command. Repeatable.            |
38	| `--limit <N>`       | 50                 | Print at most N loops.                                         |
39	| `--min-iters <N>`   | 1                  | Drop loops with fewer than N iterations (hot-loop threshold).  |
40	| `--objdump <path>`  | auto               | Override objdump (for `function+offset` and disassembly).      |
41	| `--addr2line <path>`| auto               | Override addr2line (for source-line resolution).               |
42	| `--no-source`       | off                | Skip source resolution even if DWARF is present.               |
43	| `--raw`             | off                | Print raw plugin output (CSV-ish), no formatting.              |
44	| `--optimize-rvv`    | on                 | Only report loops that contain at least one RVV instruction.   |
45	| `--no-optimize-rvv` | off                | Disable the RVV-only filter; report all loops.                 |
46	| `--llm`             | on                 | Emit a Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption (see below).  |
47	| `--no-llm`          | off                | Emit the plain human-readable table instead of the LLM report. |
48	
49	### Build prerequisites
50	
51	The plugin lives in `qemu_plugin/`. Build once:
52	
53	```
54	make -C qemu_plugin
55	```
56	
57	It is incremental on subsequent edits to `hotloops.c`. The QEMU binaries
58	themselves (`qemu-system-riscv64`, `qemu-system-riscv32`) do **not** need
59	to be rebuilt.
60	
61	## How it detects a loop
62	
63	For every translated block, the plugin remembers the PC of its last
64	instruction. When the next-executed block starts at a PC `<=` that
65	remembered PC, the transition is a backward edge - i.e. a loop iteration.
66	The pair `(header_pc, tail_pc)` is the key; the count is the number of
67	iterations.
68	
69	This catches every loop a real backward branch closes (for/while/do-while,
70	goto, manually unrolled tails, etc.) without needing to model branch
71	semantics.
72	
73	Caveat: each iteration counted is one *taken* backward branch. A loop
74	that runs N times has N-1 taken backward branches plus one fall-through
75	on exit, so the reported count is N-1 per call to the enclosing function.
76	
77	## Output modes
78	
79	Three output modes, in order of layered post-processing:
80	
81	1. `--llm` (default on) - Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption.
82	2. `--no-llm` - plain human-readable table.
83	3. `--raw` - unformatted plugin output (overrides the above).
84	
85	### LLM report (default)
86	
87	The tool emits a single Markdown document structured so an LLM (or a
88	reader skimming top-down) can answer "what is the hottest loop?" from the
89	first paragraph, then drill down via stable IDs.
90

# hotloops - hot inner-loop detector

Detects the hottest loops in a baremetal RISC-V ELF by observing backward
translation-block transitions in `qemu-system-<arch>`. For each detected
loop you get the loop header PC, the backward-branch PC, and the iteration
count. With DWARF, you also get the source `file:line`. With objdump
present, you get RVV-only filtering and per-loop disassembly context.

Two parts ship together:

- `qemu_plugin/hotloops.c` - QEMU TCG plugin that records edges.
- `build/hotloops` - C++ tool (source `driver/hotloops.cpp`) that runs the
  plugin and formats output.

## Usage

```
build/hotloops [options] <elf>
```

The tool launches `qemu-system-<arch>` with `-bios <elf>` on a baremetal
machine (default `andes_ae350`) and a vector-capable CPU (default
`andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024`). Override per the options below
for other targets.

### Options

| Flag                | Default            | Description                                                    |
|---------------------|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `--arch <a>`        | auto               | Target arch: `riscv32`, `riscv64`, or `auto` (from `file`).    |
| `--qemu <path>`     | auto               | Override the `qemu-system-<arch>` binary.                      |
| `--plugin <path>`   | auto               | Override the plugin `.so`.                                     |
| `--machine <name>`  | `andes_ae350`      | `-M <name>` passed to QEMU.                                    |
| `--cpu <spec>`      | `andes-ax45mpv,...`| `-cpu <spec>` passed to QEMU. Default enables RVV 1.0 vlen=1024.|
| `--qemu-config <f>` | -                  | `-readconfig <file>` (e.g. AE350 device cfg).                  |
| `--cwd <dir>`       | -                  | `chdir` before launching QEMU (so semihosting `fread` of `bin/*.bin` resolves). |
| `--qemu-arg <arg>`  | -                  | Extra arg appended to the QEMU command. Repeatable.            |
| `--limit <N>`       | 50                 | Print at most N loops.                                         |
| `--min-iters <N>`   | 1                  | Drop loops with fewer than N iterations (hot-loop threshold).  |
| `--objdump <path>`  | auto               | Override objdump (for `function+offset` and disassembly).      |
| `--addr2line <path>`| auto               | Override addr2line (for source-line resolution).               |
| `--no-source`       | off                | Skip source resolution even if DWARF is present.               |
| `--raw`             | off                | Print raw plugin output (CSV-ish), no formatting.              |
| `--optimize-rvv`    | on                 | Only report loops that contain at least one RVV instruction.   |
| `--no-optimize-rvv` | off                | Disable the RVV-only filter; report all loops.                 |
| `--llm`             | on                 | Emit a Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption (see below).  |
| `--no-llm`          | off                | Emit the plain human-readable table instead of the LLM report. |

### Build prerequisites

The plugin lives in `qemu_plugin/`. Build once:

```
make -C qemu_plugin
```

It is incremental on subsequent edits to `hotloops.c`. The QEMU binaries
themselves (`qemu-system-riscv64`, `qemu-system-riscv32`) do **not** need
to be rebuilt.

## How it detects a loop

For every translated block, the plugin remembers the PC of its last
instruction. When the next-executed block starts at a PC `<=` that
remembered PC, the transition is a backward edge - i.e. a loop iteration.
The pair `(header_pc, tail_pc)` is the key; the count is the number of
iterations.

This catches every loop a real backward branch closes (for/while/do-while,
goto, manually unrolled tails, etc.) without needing to model branch
semantics.

Caveat: each iteration counted is one *taken* backward branch. A loop
that runs N times has N-1 taken backward branches plus one fall-through
on exit, so the reported count is N-1 per call to the enclosing function.

## Output modes

Three output modes, in order of layered post-processing:

1. `--llm` (default on) - Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption.
2. `--no-llm` - plain human-readable table.
3. `--raw` - unformatted plugin output (overrides the above).

### LLM report (default)

The tool emits a single Markdown document structured so an LLM (or a
reader skimming top-down) can answer "what is the hottest loop?" from the
first paragraph, then drill down via stable IDs.

Layout:

- Header block: `target`, `total_iters`, `reported_loops`, `min_iters`,
  `rvv_filter`.
- `## TL;DR` paragraph naming the hottest loop, its function and source
  line, percentage of total iterations, RVV vs scalar (with the top-K
  unique vector mnemonics seen), and nesting status.
- One `### L<N>` fact-sheet per reported loop (sorted by iters desc):
  - `iters` and `pc_range` (`0xstart .. 0xend  (size: N B)`).
  - `function` (`fn+0xoff -> fn+0xoff`).
  - `source` (`file:line` or `file:line -> file:line` if the header and
    tail map to different lines).
  - `code` - inline best-effort source snippet read from the path stored
    in DWARF.
  - `rvv` summary plus `rvv_insns:` listing (capped at 8) with each
    `0xpc  mnemonic operands`.
  - `parent` / `children` - stable IDs of containing / contained loops.
    Inferred from PC-range containment, so this captures only
    same-function nesting.
  - `calls` - direct callees inside the loop body (`jal`/`jalr` with a
    statically known target via the `<name>` annotation). Indirect calls
    show as `(indirect)`.

The TL;DR is templated from the same data fields the per-loop blocks use;
no LLM call is made by the tool itself.

Limitations:

- Same-function nesting only. A caller's hot loop that calls a callee
  containing its own hot loop will show as two unrelated loops; follow
  `calls:` to bridge.
- `code:` snippets require the source file to be reachable at the
  absolute path stored in DWARF. Cross-compiled or relocated builds may
  fall back to just `file:line`.
- The RVV filter is mnemonic-based: any insn whose mnemonic begins with
  `v<alpha>` (e.g. `vsetvli`, `vle32.v`, `vadd.vv`, `vmul.vv`). Standard
  scalar RISC-V has no such mnemonic, so this is exact in practice.

### Table mode (`--no-llm`)

Header line, then a fixed-width table sorted by `iters` descending:

```
# hot loops (iters >= <threshold>[, RVV-only]), sorted desc, top <K>
iters | start_pc           -> end_pc             | location              | source
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
<n>   | 0x<16-hex>         -> 0x<16-hex>         | <fn>+0x<o> -> <fn>+0x<o> | file:line -> file:line
...
```

Columns:

- `iters`     - taken backward-branch count (sorted desc).
- `start_pc`  - PC of the loop header (the branch target).
- `end_pc`    - PC of the backward branch (the loop tail).
- `location`  - `function+offset -> function+offset` from the ELF symbol
                table. Shows `?` if the address is not inside any sized
                FUNC symbol.
- `source`    - `file:line -> file:line` from DWARF (basenamed).
                Collapsed to a single `file:line` when both ends map to
                the same source line. Only present when the ELF has debug
                info and `--no-source` is not set.

### Raw mode (`--raw`)

Bypasses both the LLM report and the table, printing the unformatted
plugin output:

```
hotloops: <distinct> distinct backward edges, <hot> hot (>= <thr> iters), sorted by iterations desc
start_pc, end_pc, iterations
0x..., 0x..., <n>
...
```

Stable across releases - useful for piping into another tool.

## Example

A doubly-nested loop with an RVV inner body:

```c
/* hotloops_demo.c - baremetal entry */
#include <stdint.h>

__attribute__((noinline))
static int dot_rvv(const int *a, const int *b, int n) {
    int s = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += a[i] * b[i];   /* line 6, vectorized */
    return s;
}

void main(void) {
    static int a[64], b[64];
    for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) { a[i] = i; b[i] = 64 - i; }
    long total = 0;
    for (int outer = 0; outer < 500; outer++)
        total += dot_rvv(a, b, 64);                  /* 64 * 500 inner iters */
    (void)total;
}
```

Build for AE350 with the Andes RISC-V toolchain (or any baremetal
RVV-capable toolchain), then run:

```
$ build/hotloops --min-iters 100 --limit 5 build/hotloops_demo.elf
```

LLM-mode output (the default) looks like:

```markdown
# Hotloops Report
target:           hotloops_demo.elf
total_iters:      32000
reported_loops:   1
min_iters:        100
rvv_filter:       on

## TL;DR
Hottest loop is L1 in `dot_rvv` (hotloops_demo.c:6), 31500 iters = 98.4% of
total. Body is RVV (vsetvli, vle32.v, vmul.vv, +1 more). It is top-level
(no parent loop), and contains no inner loop.

## Loops

### L1 [hottest]  (98.4% of total)
iters:        31500
pc_range:     0x80000200 .. 0x80000218  (size: 24 B)
function:     dot_rvv+0x10 -> dot_rvv+0x28
source:       hotloops_demo.c:6
code:         for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += a[i] * b[i];   /* line 6, vectorized */
rvv:          yes (4 insns)
rvv_insns:
  - 0x80000200  vsetvli    t0,a2,e32,m1,ta,ma
  - 0x80000208  vle32.v    v1,(a0)
  - 0x8000020c  vmul.vv    v2,v1,v3
  - 0x80000210  vadd.vv    v4,v4,v2
parent:       -
children:     []
calls:        []
```

Reading the report:

- The TL;DR alone identifies the hot path: `dot_rvv` line 6, 98.4% of all
  taken backward branches, RVV-vectorized.
- `iters = 31500` is close to the expected `64 * 500 = 32000`; the missing
  500 are the per-call exits (last iter of `dot_rvv` falls through instead
  of branching back).
- The 500-iter outer loop in `main` was filtered out by `--min-iters 100`.
  It would also have been filtered by the default RVV-only filter since
  `main`'s body is scalar (drop with `--no-optimize-rvv` to see scalar
  loops too).

For piping into a different tool, use `--raw`:

```
$ build/hotloops --raw build/hotloops_demo.elf | head
hotloops: 1 distinct backward edges, 1 hot (>= 1 iters), sorted by iterations desc
start_pc, end_pc, iterations
0x0000000080000200, 0x0000000080000218, 31500
```

## Tips

- Strip rarely-interesting startup loops by raising `--min-iters` to a
  value above your background noise floor (e.g. `--min-iters 1000` for a
  workload that runs your hot path millions of times).
- For a very short workload, lower `--min-iters` and raise `--limit`
  to see the full distribution.
- Default settings filter to RVV-containing loops only; pair with
  `--no-optimize-rvv` if you also want to see the scalar hot spots
  (e.g. an outer driver loop wrapping a vectorized kernel).
- For LLM consumption, pipe the default output straight into your prompt
  - the TL;DR is in the first ~10 lines and the per-loop blocks are
  cross-referenceable by their `L<N>` IDs.
- `--raw` is the stable interface for downstream tooling.

6	## Repository Overview
7	
8	Andes hybrid RISC-V simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz-level) + vsim (SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) share architectural state across a magic-CSR boundary. 13	  there is one source of truth.

93	## Architecture
94	
95	### Two-Phase Handoff
96	
97	```
98	QEMU1 --(state file + shared mmap)--> vsim (resume + run ROI + drain)
99	```
100	
101	1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On the marker trigger (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
102	2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
103	3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands, one write per register. Every CSR write -- the base M-mode scalars, the Andes V5 block, and the M-ext block -- also goes through Abstract Commands only, one write per CSR; there is no batched Program-Buffer sweep anywhere in the register/CSR transport, in either direction (a WARL/read-only CSR faulting mid-batch can't be tolerated the way the abstract path's per-CSR cmderr-clear can). `StateDrain` mirrors this: one abstract read per GPR/FPR/CSR. The Program Buffer carries only state the abstract command space cannot reach: the V-data sweep, `vtype`+`vl` (Tier B, see V-State Transport below), and the L2C MMIO window. **Liveness gate**: restores whose drained value equals the engine's own reset value are skipped (a no-op write; each DM op costs ~200-900 simulated cycles). The reset baseline is drained once per (engine build, ELF) on the first hybrid run and cached under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/`; `--no-reset-baseline` disables. Never gated: mstatus, GPRs, dpc, dcsr, mcycle, minstret, the S/U PMP mirror. Verify-transparent by construction (skip only when the value is already there).
104	4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands into `hybrid_state_v1`. This is the end of the run: the cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` minus QEMU1's drained `mcycle`. The old QEMU2 resume leg was removed entirely.
105	
106	**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes the CSRs the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mscratch` (L23), `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip` (L24), `mcycle`, `minstret`, `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags, gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`; L20), and the Andes machine-setup CSRs `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) + `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) (L21). The cache pair matters for the cycle figure, not correctness: crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via `mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional engine, so without transporting it vsim resumes at the ROI with caches at their reset default (disabled) and the whole window runs uncached -- inflating the cycle count severalfold. All are tolerant writes: an engine without a given custom CSR mirrors the write as a no-op. In the trap-free ROI these writable M-mode CSRs are ordinary read/write state, so they round-trip fully: restored at resume, re-read at drain (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`), and compared by `--verify` (`state_diff`). Two verify-side exceptions: `mip` is restored + re-read but NOT compared -- its pending bits are hardware/platform-driven (the timer bit tracks elapsed time, which advances differently in QEMU's functional clock vs vsim's cycle clock), so comparing it would false-positive; and `mtvec` is restored but not re-drained. The S/U trap CSRs `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` are drained by the plugin since v1 and, since the ax66 registration (option A), restored + re-read + `--verify`-compared on S-mode-capable engines (caps gate SMODE; the describe list names them); on an M-only engine (`ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) they stay drain-record-only. Other S-mode CSRs (`sstatus`, `sepc`, ...) remain deferred to the S/U-envelope work. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free, interrupt-free, and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.
107	
108	**Privilege (L6)**: the handoff carries the real privilege level. The plugin drains the gdbstub `priv` register, `ResumeDriver` read-modify-writes `dcsr.prv` before `dret` (and verifies the write took -- an M-mode-only RTL like the default `ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`, WARL-pins the field, and the resume aborts with a pick-an-S/U-capable-engine error), and `StateDrain` reads `dcsr.prv` back at the exit halt. For S/U handoffs the producer's PMP block (64 `pmpaddr` + the 8 even `pmpcfg`) is also mirrored into the hart, because with PMP implemented and no matching entry every S/U access faults; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only (L2). The `rt_priv_smode`/`rt_priv_umode` fixtures run on the S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66` (see `scripts/run_e2e.sh`); the ROI itself must still be trap-free, single-privilege, and paging-off (S-mode CSRs are not transported).
109	
110	### Trigger Modes
111	
112	The repo ships 2 switching modes (triggers); each measures one region you
113	choose. The C++ `andesim` driver exposes them via `--trigger marker|pc`.
114	
115	- **marker mode** (default): Pattern-matches `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (entry) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (exit) at retire time. The markers are RISC-V HINTs (rd=x0 discards the result), i.e. architectural NOPs -- a marker binary also runs standalone on every engine and on silicon. Users get them from `<andesim/ROI.h>` (`andesim_ROI_begin()/end()`).
116	- **PC mode**: explicit boundary PCs passed as `--pc-start S --pc-end E` (symbol name or `0x` address) resolved at startup; marker insns are bypassed. Both args are required.
117	
118	`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker|pc` is the unified orchestrator; `tests/e2e.sh` drives marker/pc internally. The run yields a cycle figure: window cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta (`hybrid_state_v1::mcycle`).
119	
120	### Shared ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`)
121	
122	`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between the QEMU plugin and vsim. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, fcsr, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr), (v3) the Andes V5 CSR block `struct hybrid_andes_csr andes`, (v4) the writable M-mode CSR block `struct hybrid_m_ext_csr m_ext`, and (v5) the L2C MMIO register window `struct hybrid_l2c l2c`. `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=128` supports VLEN up to 1024 bits; the live width is the runtime `vlenb`, and a producer whose vlenb exceeds the ceiling refuses to drain instead of truncating (L11). Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.
123	
124	**v3 Andes block**: `struct hybrid_andes_csr` carries the Andes-specific CSRs a bare-metal Andes core sets up before the ROI -- 13 scalar CSRs (mxstatus, mpft_ctl, mclk_ctl, milmb, mdlmb, mecc_code, mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base, mcountermask_m, uitb, jvt, ucode) + PMA (pmacfg[2] @ 0xBC0/0xBC2, pmaaddr[16] @ 0xBD0..0xBDF). The 13 scalars are defined ONCE by the X-macro `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)` in `state_abi.h`, which every consumer iterates (plugin drain, `ResumeDriver` restore, `StateDrain` re-read, driver `state_diff` verify) -- so adding a CSR is one line, no consumer drifts. Live only when `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES` is set (the plugin sets it when QEMU's gdbstub advertised at least one Andes CSR). All restores are tolerant (a core lacking the CSR no-ops the write); the block round-trips through the trap-free ROI and is `--verify`-compared, except `msp_bound`/`msp_base` (HW stack-protection bounds) and `milmb`/`mdlmb` (ILM/DLM base+enable) which are engine-reset-divergent -- QEMU resets `msp_bound`/`msp_base` to all-ones (a vsim core without HW stack protection drains 0), and drains the `milmb`/`mdlmb` enable bit clear while the vsim RTL drains it set -- so they are verify-excluded like `mip`.
125	
126	**v5 L2C block**: `struct hybrid_l2c` carries the **L2 cache controller's MMIO register window** (`reg[]` = offsets 0x0000..0x0527, DS220 11.8.5 Table 112). Unlike every other block this is DEVICE MMIO, not a CSR: the plugin drains the whole window with `qemu_plugin_read_memory_hwaddr` (physical address `l2c_base`, default 0xE0500000), and `ResumeDriver::restore_l2c` writes back ONLY the writable boot-static config registers -- Control (0x0008: `CEN` enable + prefetch + ECC + RAM timing), HPM Control (0x0010), Way Allocation Masks (0x0300..0x0328) -- via Program-Buffer word stores (`sw`, per DS220 11.8.3's <8-byte access rule). The read-only Configuration Register, the side-effecting CCTL command registers (writing one re-issues an L2 cache op), and the W1C error registers are captured but never restored. `StateDrain::drain_l2c` re-reads the config registers (`lwu`) for `--verify` (`state_diff` compares `l2c.ctrl` with the RO INITSTATUS[14] bit masked). This is the MMIO analog of the `mcache_ctl` (L1-enable) transport, and matters for the cycle figure the same way: an L2-enabled engine that resumed with L2 disabled would run the ROI severalfold slower. **Restore is HARD-gated on the engine having an L2C** (`Simulator::l2c_present()` from `_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB > 0`): a store to an absent L2C region faults the Program Buffer, unlike a tolerant CSR write. Every current engine is built `NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0`, so the block is transported forward-looking and the restore/drain no-op today. QEMU seeds the L2C Control Register's reset value (`CEN=1`, DS220 11.8.7) at machine init (`andes_ae350.c`), so a guest that relies on the default is not drained as `CEN=0`.
127	
128	**v6 write-mask**: `write_mask[2]` (one bit per mask-governed config CSR, slot map + decode helpers in `include/hybrid/write_mask.h`, live under `HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK`) records **which CSRs the guest actually WROTE** during the QEMU phase. The plugin decodes CSR-write instructions at translation time (`csrrw`/`csrrwi` always write; `csrrs/c` only when rs1!=x0; `csrrsi/ci` only when uimm!=0) and registers an exec callback only on instructions that write a mask-governed CSR -- steady-state code carries zero instrumentation, so the fast leg is unaffected. Consumers (`ResumeDriver` restore, `state_diff` verify) skip any governed CSR whose bit is clear: an untouched CSR's drained value is only QEMU's reset default, which can legitimately differ from the engine's RTL reset value (`msp_bound` all-ones vs 0, `milmb.IEN` 0 vs 1), so skipping keeps the engine at ITS OWN reset value -- what real silicon of that engine would hold -- and makes producer/engine reset divergence harmless by construction for every current and future engine, with no per-engine data in QEMU. Governed set: the v3 Andes scalars + PMA, the v4 M-ext block, `mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl`. Never governed: GPRs/FPRs/V, mstatus, dpc/dcsr, counters, fcsr, the trap-writable CSRs (mepc/mcause/mtval/mip/mie -- hardware writes them without a CSR insn), mtvec/mscratch, and PMP (the S/U mirror is a correctness requirement). `ucode` is transport-always (DSP ops set its sticky OV flag without a CSR insn). Flag clear (pre-v6 file) -> consumers fall back to restore/compare-everything.
129	
130	**Memory-content sidecars (NOT in `hybrid_state_v1`)**: ILM/DLM and HVM content travels OUTSIDE the state struct, as raw binary sidecar files next to each state file. The plugin (args `ilm_size`/`dlm_size`/`hvm_size` in bytes; bases default `0xA0000000`/`0xA0200000`/`0x90000000`) drains `<state>.ilm/.dlm/.hvm` through the slave-port/subordinate apertures; the vsim leg backdoor-loads them (`--ilm/--dlm/--hvm` -- zero-sim-cycle Verilator hierarchical-reference pokes into the RTL SRAMs, NOT the DM Program Buffer); the exit drain dumps the read-duals next to the handoff-out state. Armed by the engine's `--describe` sizes (`ilm_size`/`dlm_size`/`hvm_size`, bytes; 0 = no memory or wrapper lacks the set_*/get_* backdoor pair -- capability-gated so a config-has-it/wrapper-can't engine arms nothing). These QEMU memories are per-CPU overlays (LM) or standalone RAM (HVM), NOT backed by the shared mmap, so the sidecars are the only road their content travels; QEMU's raw geometry must be synced (`-readconfig` on the driver path, `-global` in tests/e2e.sh -- HVM's property is `hvm_size_pow_2`, log2) because QEMU's compiled-in defaults (2 MB ILM at 0x0, 1-BYTE HVM) are wrong for every engine.
131	
132	Flags (`HYBRID_FLAG_RV64`, `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`, `HYBRID_FLAG_V`, `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES`, `HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT`, `HYBRID_FLAG_L2C`, `HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK`) gate which state blocks are live. The ABI struct is validated by `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp` (in the external vsim repo).
133	
134	### V-State Transport
135	
136	V data registers (v0..v31) move through a scratch region in the shared mmap.
137	L26: that region is the mmap's TOP page, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) =
138	ram_base + ram_size - HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`, NOT a fixed address. The driver
139	maps one page more than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes`), so the
140	scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size`, just above the program's RAM, where no
141	program layout can collide with it (`cmd_run` also rejects an ELF whose static
142	image would reach into it). `ResumeDriver`/`StateDrain` take the GPA as a
143	required-when-V argument (the simulator passes `v_scratch_gpa()`); a V handoff
144	with it unset throws. vsim drives the transfer via the Debug Module **Program
145	Buffer** while the hart is halted, so benchmark binaries issue no transport code:
146	- `stage_v_to_scratch` copies `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` into the scratch region
147	  before resume; `ResumeDriver` then sweeps `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch into the
148	  regfile (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=true).
149	- At drain, `StateDrain` sweeps `vse8.v v0..v31` from the regfile back to scratch
150	  (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=false); `read_v_from_scratch` lifts the bytes into
151	  `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` (the drained handoff file; there is no QEMU2 ship step).
152	
153	Each sweep leads with `vsetvl` to e8/m8 (vl=8*vlenb), which also forces vstart=0;
154	with LMUL=8 one `vle8.v`/`vse8.v` moves a group of 8 registers, so all 32 move in
155	4 grouped ops in a single Program-Buffer execution. The scratch is packed at the
156	RUNTIME vlenb stride (`stage_v_to_scratch` drops the wire-format
157	`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX` padding so each 8-register group is contiguous).
158	
159	V scalar CSR transport (vtype, vl, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr):
160	- **Tier A** (Abstract Commands): vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, mstatus.VS
161	- **Tier B** (Program Buffer): vtype + vl via `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` (direct CSR write to vtype sets vill; vl is read-only; only `vsetvl` restores both atomically)
162	
163	Restore order in `ResumeDriver::resume()` when `HYBRID_FLAG_V` is set:
164	1. `mstatus.VS` (enables V in the hart)
165	2. V-data reload sweep: `vsetvl` e8/m8 then `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch in the
166	   Program Buffer. Runs BEFORE the architectural V-CSR restore (whose `vsetvl`
167	   overwrites the sweep's vtype/vl/vstart) and uses x5/x6/x7 as scratch.
168	3. `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` in Program Buffer (stages `vl` in x5, `vtype` in x6 via abstract GPR writes first)
169	4. `vstart` (AFTER vsetvl: vsetvl resets vstart to 0)
170	5. `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr`
171	6. GPR loop (overwrites the x5/x6/x7 scratch - safe now)
172	
173	`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough()` issues the matching `vse8.v` dump sweep
174	LAST, after every architectural read (GPRs/FPRs/V-CSRs/mcycle/minstret), so the
175	sweep's clobbers and any counter increments cannot corrupt the drained state.
176	
177	### Test Fixtures
178	
179	All fixtures run on the unified `tests/e2e.sh` harness, which
180	sets up an `/dev/shm`-backed shared mmap (128 MB) so memory survives
181	the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. Three fixture families:
182	
183	| Family   | Examples                                                    | Notes |
184	|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------|
185	| asm      | `handoff_roundtrip`, `rt_all_gprs`, `rt_csr_survival`, `rt_shared_mem` | no C runtime; don't strictly need shared mmap but use it anyway (~20 ms cost is negligible). |
186	| C-level  | `rt_c_hello`, `rt_c_matmul`, `rt_c_v_regs`, `rt_c_v_csrs`   | hybrid round-trip tests, linked through the vplat runtime (below). Shared mmap is REQUIRED -- vsim resumes on QEMU1's memory, so the stack/heap and `main()`'s frame must survive the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. |
187	| vplat    | `vplat_hello`, `vplat_exit41`, `vplat_file`                 | smoke tests for the runtime's own features (exit code, file io). The runtime is engine-portable, shipped as `build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a` (sources in `runtime/`; build with `make -C runtime` or `scripts/build_all.sh runtime`): UART stdio + SimControl exit + HTIF file io, NO semihosting -- the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid. Users link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`. See docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 4; smoke tests in `tests/vplat/`. |
188	
189	The shared mmap is created with `mktemp -p /dev/shm` + `truncate`,
190	then QEMU is launched with `-object memory-backend-file`.
191	
192	Fixture source lives in `tests/fixtures/`; the shared runtime sources live at the repo root in `runtime/`. ALL C fixtures (rt_c_* and vplat_*) link through the shipped vplat runtime with the user command (`-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`); nothing in-tree links `-lgloss_vh` or uses semihosting syscalls anymore (asm fixtures still carry a semihosting exit fallback from `semihost_exit.inc`). V-using fixtures require `-march=rv64gcv`. Syscalls bottom out in MMIO devices both engines model (UART2 `0xf0300000`, SimControl/HTIF `0xe0080000` -- QEMU side is inline in `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c`), so a `printf` inside the ROI works on every engine (it just adds the real UART cycles to the figure); the old "Phase-2 no-syscall rule" survives only as a measurement-hygiene convention in cycle-measuring fixtures, and as a hard rule for user binaries that still link a semihosting libgloss. The ROI markers are HINT NOPs, so vplat binaries may carry them (`<andesim/ROI.h>`, installed to `build/runtime/include/`) and still run standalone on every engine; binaries you cannot edit delimit the ROI with PC symbols and `--trigger pc` instead.
193	
194	## Key Files
195	
196	| File | Purpose |
197	|------|---------|
198	| `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` | Wire-format struct (shared by all three components) |
199	| `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` | TCG plugin: drain on trigger |
200	| `src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp` (vsim repo) | Phase dispatcher |
201	| `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` (vsim repo) | DMI state restore (Tier A+B) |
